head: pr17399-r3
report:
I found one defect, and I measured it. While `/pause` holds a request, that request keeps a cross-process provider in-flight slot for the whole pause. Any other omp process that uses the same provider waits for as long as a person leaves the first one paused. I would fix this before merge. # Wait out the pause before taking the provider in-flight slot, not after **File / line:** `packages/ai/src/stream.ts:690-701`, in `withProviderInFlightLimit`. The patch adds `await holdBeforeDispatch(hold, options?.signal)` after `release = await acquireProviderInFlightSlot(...)`. **Mechanism.** - `acquireProviderInFlightSlot` takes a lease in a lock directory on disk, shared by every omp process on the machine. While the lease is held, a heartbeat refreshes it every 5 s (`PROVIDER_INFLIGHT_HEARTBEAT_MS`), so the 30 s stale-lease reaper (`PROVIDER_INFLIGHT_LEASE_STALE_MS`) never removes it. - The patch then parks on `beforeDispatch` while holding that lease. During `/pause` this is `agentPauseGate.dispatchHold(...)`, or the agent loop's `waitForProcessPause`, and nothing ends it except a human resuming. The transport-fetch hold at `utils/transport-fetch.ts:159` also runs inside the dispatch, so it holds the slot too. - With `providers.

.maxConcurrency` / `maxInFlightRequests` set (the ollama-cloud case cited at `session-maintenance.ts:3725-3732`), a paused session's compaction, side turn, title or memory request, or its re-dispatch, keeps the slot for the whole pause. Every unpaused omp process using that provider then blocks in `acquireProviderInFlightSlot`. - Before this patch, the pause was polled before `streamSimple`, so nothing parked while holding a lease. - The code comment says the order is deliberate: "Last, so the slot wait above cannot outlast it". That avoids a pause slipping in during the slot wait, but in exchange the pause outlasts the slot. - Fix: also hold before acquiring the slot, and keep the post-acquire hold only as a re-check. Alternatively, release the lease and re-acquire it if the post-acquire hold actually parks. **Trigger.** There are two processes that share one in-flight root, with `maxInFlightRequests: { tests: 1 }`: - **Child process:** calls `streamSimple(mockModel, ctx, { maxInFlightRequests: { tests: 1 }, beforeDispatch: () => new Promise(() => {}) })`, which stands in for a `/pause` that is never released. - **Parent process:** has no pause and issues the same request with the same limit. It waits 40 s, which is beyond the 30 s stale-lease threshold. Probe files: `scratch/.../r1/slot-child.ts` and `scratch/.../r1/slot.test.ts`. Both drive the real `streamSimple` and `__providerInFlightForTesting.setRoot` from the snapshot. ``` cd heads/670df28f7bf7/packages/ai && bun test /slot.test.ts ``` **Measured:** ``` CHILD held (paused) at 1793342863700 PARENT (not paused) after 40019ms: STILL WAITING lease dir entries: [ "WYMOvDpBhBEFZr8aKQ0IRz39y9SSzkmLFM0aXi-i5EE/282307-1793342863698-430ebc31-b804-488d-b5f8-b52a9cc1e164", "WYMOvDpBhBEFZr8aKQ0IRz39y9SSzkmLFM0aXi-i5EE/282307-1793342863698-430ebc31-b804-488d-b5f8-b52a9cc1e164/info.json", "WYMOvDpBhBEFZr8aKQ0IRz39y9SSzkmLFM0aXi-i5EE" ] 1 pass ``` After 40 s, the paused child's lease (pid 282307) is still live and the unpaused parent has not dispatched. The heartbeat keeps the lease fresh, so the parent's wait has no bound. **Priority: P1.** This is an unbounded wait under load: pausing one session starves every other omp process that uses the same rate-limited provider. # Hypotheses I checked and dropped (not defects) - **The "live" transport-build hold accumulation in `transportFetch`:** no production caller passes `wrapTransport`, so no build is ever live. - **The gemini-cli first-event watchdog running during a transport-level hold:** that provider sets `providerHandlesFirstEventTimeouts`, so `firstItemTimeoutMs` is 0, and the pre-response guard it does arm is suspended by `transportFetch`. **Verdict:** not safe to merge as is. A paused request keeps its cross-process provider in-flight slot for the whole pause, so other processes using that provider wait indefinitely.
